text.title: Graph / Tree / Flat Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing tree from observable data properties to a structure choice. Most real systems terminate at the first two branches.

decision-tree.root-question: Does any node belong to more than one independent parent, OR do references jump between unrelated subtrees, OR are there cycles, OR do relations expire over time?

conclusion.verdict: STOP. No graph. If the data nests, use a hierarchy with compact indexes; if it does not, use flat retrieval with reranking. Record `warrant: none` and close the record.

branch.when: none_of_the_four == false AND graph_tokens_per_query >= incumbent_tokens_per_query AND accuracy_gain_measured == false

conclusion.verdict: STOP. Warrant exists but does not pay. Keep the incumbent structure; revisit when query mix shifts toward multi-hop.
Build the graph from derived edges only (imports, links, refs, foreign keys, git). Declare the closed edge enum. Do NOT invoke LLM extraction in v1 — ship the free graph and measure what it misses.

branch.when: none_of_the_four == false AND structural_sources_available == false AND corpus_is_static == true

conclusion.verdict: LLM extraction is permitted. Name each extracted edge class and why derivation is impossible. Budget construction as a one-off; a static corpus amortises it.

branch.when: none_of_the_four == false AND structural_sources_available == false AND corpus_is_static == false

conclusion.verdict: High risk. Extraction cost is repaid on every change. Prototype on a corpus slice, measure rebuild cost against change frequency, and prefer a lazy pattern that indexes like flat retrieval and pays graph cost only at query time.
Overlay, not alternative: whichever branch above applies, edges MUST be bitemporal — expire on contradiction, never delete, filter by validity at query time.
Mark `status: draft`. An unvalidated graph converts data rot into confident wrong answers; it is not shippable regardless of how good the retrieval looks.
